title: Operator Assistant: command shelf & incident shortcuts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a lightweight "operator assistant" that exposes a curated set of admin commands, one-click runbook tasks, and incident shortcuts to support engineers via the ops CLI and Console quick-actions. This is aimed at reducing time-to-first-action during incidents and ensuring runbooks are executed with consistent telemetry and RBAC checks.
background: Current situation: multiple ad-hoc admin scripts live in GH gists and private repos. Responders open a mix of runbook docs and shell commands during incidents which causes variability (missing flags, inconsistent logging, manual audit steps). We want a small opinionated surface: a command shelf (predefined safe actions), taskified runbook steps (preflight checks + prompts), and automatic telemetry/audit events for every invocation.
scope: In-scope: (1) CLI and Console quick-action definitions for ~12 high-frequency ops actions (rotate-key, clear-cache, bump-queue, restart-worker-group, collect-profile, promote-canary), (2) runbooks-as-tasks wrapper that enforces prechecks (RBAC, circuit-breaker, capacity check), (3) consistent telemetry events (who, what, outcome, duration) sent to internal analytics and linked to the incident ID, (4) minimal safety gating (confirmations and optional canary tags), (5) docs + small training exercise.
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of runbook library, GUI overhaul of Console, or on-prem packaging. We'll integrate with existing runbook store but not migrate all legacy playbooks in this ticket.
design_decisions: 1) Commands will be YAML-declarative (name, safe-mode flags, required roles, prechecks, post-hooks) stored in repo 'infra/operator-shelf'. 2) CLI invocation will call a central 'ops-assistant' service that enforces RBAC and emits a single audit event; shell actions are executed via bounded Lambdas / job runners to avoid long-lived session shells. 3) Telemetry schema will follow existing ops_event.{actor,action,target,outcome,duration,incident_id}. 4) For high-risk actions (restart, migrate), require two-step confirmation or a second approver flag for P0 incidents.
notes: We intentionally keep the first ship to a narrow set of actions to get telemetry and safety right. Future work will add templated arguments and multi-step transactions.
acceptance_criteria: 12 predefined commands available in both CLI and Console quick-actions
Each invocation emits an ops_event with actor, action, target, outcome, duration, and incident_id
RBAC enforced: only members of roles listed in command YAML can execute
Runbooks executed through 'tasks' record step-by-step logs and can be replayed for postmortem
Unit and integration tests for prechecks and audit emission included
Documentation page + 1-hour lab for on-call rotation included

postmortem_plan: If we see more than 3 denied-attempt anomalies in a day after ship, pause widening rollout and optionally rollback specific commands. Add more granular grants and audit views. Iterate with Support to refine confirmations and help text.
final_notes: This ticket focuses on predictable, auditable operator actions rather than full automation. The user-experience goal is to remove context-switching from responders and provide a single source of truth for safe admin operations. We'll follow up with metrics (MTTA reduction, task success rate) in the release retrospective.
